whatItIs.text: An elongated fruit, botanically a berry, from a giant herbaceous plant; dessert bananas are eaten raw, and the cooking kind are called plantains.

historyNote.text: Wild Musa are native to tropical Indomalaya and Australia and were probably domesticated in New Guinea; the Cavendish type that dominates Western shelves is a single seedless variety that disease breeders keep racing to replace.

howToChoose.text: Choose firm, evenly coloured fruit for eating over several days; brown freckles mean sweeter, softer flesh, which is ideal for baking.

storage.text: Keep at room temperature away from other fruit; refrigerating a ripe banana blackens the peel but holds the fruit inside.

useItUp.text: Black bananas are baking bananas: banana bread, pancakes, or blended from frozen into nice cream.

substitutions.note: in baking, for moisture and binding; milder flavour and less structure
